title: Come for Sha
thesis: The live read settled what this account actually is: seven of her ten best reels have Sha herself on camera, and one review says a client followed her for ten years across three suburbs. People are not choosing a salon, they are choosing her. So this week sells the person first, and the education, the services and the prices all hang off her. One post a day for seven days: two finished reels built frame by frame, a five-slide carousel and four single posts. There are no photographs this week — the face-free library had been used until it went stale, so every image is drawn: hair as a colourist sees it, in strands, swatches, foils and gloss.
projection: Followers held at 186 across the fortnight while 5 new posts went up — all five hers, and none from weeks 6 or 7, which means 17 authored posts went unused. Her own reels kept performing: 6.99% on the level-2-to-level-7 transformation, and the first comment in a month on the 'journey to your dream blonde' reel, which is the week-5 platinum idea rewritten in her own words. The lesson is the same one the numbers have given three times: the account rewards Sha, on video, speaking plainly. So this week ships fewer pieces and makes them finished — two reels she only has to upload, a carousel and four single posts — instead of ten she has to sort through. Target is a return to growth, 188-191 followers, and at least one of the two reels posted. What this sets up is the Caulfield Cup on Saturday 17 October: the price ladder carries the 48-hour line so race-day colour lands on Wednesday the 14th, her quietest open day.
emailNote: Hi Sha — this is the updated version of this week, and it replaces the earlier email. Every picture is new: instead of reusing the same photos again, the posts and both reels now use custom drawn artwork of hair colour — swatches, foils, gloss and balayage. There is also one extra post for Sunday, about the $45 gloss. Please use this email, not the first one. Read each caption before you post it, and change anything that does not sound like you.

posts.title: 5 things your colourist wishes you knew
posts.imageAlt: A 21.6-second vertical reel with a stories-style progress bar across the top. A cream 5 slams onto a fall of drawn gold hair, then five facts land one after another through whip, iris and slice transitions over moving illustrated hair: a blow wave lasting three to five days over glossy rose-toned waves, a 48-hour counter with a filling ring, purple shampoo struck through and revealed as a toner as a violet drop falls and a brassy lock cools to pearl, a thermometer dropping from hot to lukewarm, and a week counter running to 10-14 weeks for balayage. It closes on a colourist's shade book fanning open above an ink panel reading Save this, with price chips and a DM me to book button.
posts.whyItWorks: It is the format of her single best-performing post by rate — the 'Did you know a professional blow wave can last three to five days' reel at 9.68% with three comments — rebuilt with five facts instead of one. The progress bar is the retention device: once someone has seen two of five segments fill, leaving feels unfinished. 'Number three surprises everyone' is a promise the reel pays off with a 'Told you' sticker at fact three, so it is a hook rather than clickbait. Every fact is true and every one sells a service without an offer in it — the gloss, the midweek colour, the balayage rhythm. There are no photographs in it: the hair is drawn and animated — it falls in, sways and catches the light — so nothing reused, and nothing that pretends to be a result she did not do.

caption.hook: Five things I tell every client, in twenty seconds 🤍
caption.body: Number three is the one nobody believes until they try it.
caption.cta: Save it, then send it to the friend who washes her hair the day she gets home.

howToPost: Download the reel from the email and upload it as a reel. It is already 1080x1920 and 21.6 seconds.
It has no sound on purpose. Add a trending track in the app — something with a steady beat suits the cuts. If a song will not attach, that is the account type, so pick the next one.
Monday evening, about 7pm, when people are on the couch and scrolling properly.

posts.title: Don't book a salon. Book Sha.
posts.imageAlt: A deep fig-green card. On the right, a tall arch framed in gold holds a drawn fall of balayage hair, dark at the root and melting to gold at the ends, with a few sparkles. Behind it a giant outlined 'Sha' in clay. On the left, 'Don't book a salon.' in cream with a gold underline, and 'Book Sha.' in very large gold serif. Four cream tiles run along the foot: 20+ years behind the chair, 1000+ happy clients, K18 certified, 1 chair no hand-offs. A gold bar reads DM me to book, Sundays 11-4.
posts.whyItWorks: Seven of her ten best reels have her in them, so this is the post that states the account's actual thesis out loud. The arch echoes the round mirrors in her salon and this time it holds the colour itself — drawn balayage rather than another reuse of the same photographs. The four credential tiles are all taken from her own website, so nothing on the card is a claim she has not already made publicly.

caption.hook: You are not booking a salon. You are booking me.
caption.body: Twenty years, one chair, and the same pair of hands from the first chat to the blow wave. Nobody hands you off halfway.
caption.cta: DM me and tell me what you are after.

howToPost: Pin this one to the top of your profile. It is the answer to 'why her' for anyone who lands on the page.

posts.title: What actually happens in Sha's chair
posts.imageAlt: Five-slide carousel. The cover is a colourist's shade book fanned open across the top — seven drawn swatches from 4N espresso to 10P pearl — above the headline 'What actually happens in Sha's chair'. Four step slides follow, each with drawn art in an arch, a large outlined step numeral, three tags and a coloured CTA bar: the chat, three swatches held up to choose a shade, where you get the price first; the colour, three gold foils on a dark lock, placed by hand with no hand-offs; the toner, a violet gloss drop over toned hair, unrushed; and the finish, glossy balayage with the next date booked and the formula kept on file.
posts.whyItWorks: The biggest barrier for a new colour client is not price, it is not knowing what happens once they sit down. This walks them through it in four steps, and every step is a difference from a chain salon that her own website already states — the consultation and price before anything is mixed, one person start to finish, no double-booking. Posted on a Wednesday because it is her quietest open day and this is the post most likely to turn a browser into a first booking.

caption.hook: What actually happens when you sit in my chair.
caption.body: Four steps, one person, and nobody waiting behind you. Swipe through.
caption.cta: DM me to book yours. Wednesdays are the calm ones.

howToPost: Upload all five slides in order — the shade book first.
Save it to a highlight called 'First visit'. It answers every nervous new-client DM before it is sent.

posts.title: Come for Sha
posts.imageAlt: A 21-second vertical reel. 'Don't book a haircut.' is struck through in gold and 'Book Sha.' slams in. A whip into a fall of drawn copper hair with her name, Shamalka, revealed as a lower third. Four stat beats wipe in with a rotating ring of text: 20+ years, 1,000+ clients, K18 certified, 1 chair. A client review types itself out with a route line drawing from Malvern to Armadale to Camberwell and the line 'Some clients follow a salon. Hers follow her.' A three-by-three grid of nine drawn shades — espresso to pearl to toned violet — flies together under 'All Sha.', the menu flips in like a departures board, and it closes on a gold ring of drawn balayage under 'Come for Sha.' with a DM me to book button and a moving ticker.
posts.whyItWorks: It makes the case her own content has been making by accident: people come for her. The stats are hers from her own website and the review is quoted verbatim from a real client. The grid is nine drawn shades rather than nine reused photographs — every shade one colourist does, which is the point of the reel. The typewriter review and the route line are the two most watchable moments — motion that carries meaning, not decoration — and the flip-board menu means the reel sells the services and every price without a single discount.

caption.hook: Some clients follow a salon. Mine follow me ✨
caption.body: One of my clients has followed me from Malvern to Armadale to Camberwell. Ten years. I will never take that for granted.
caption.cta: Come for the colour, stay for the chat. DM me to book.

howToPost: Download from the email and upload as a reel. 1080x1920, no sound — add a trending track in the app.
Thursday evening, when people start planning the weekend. This is the reel most likely to be sent to a friend.

posts.title: Pick your step
posts.imageAlt: An ink card with a faint gold sunburst. 'Pick your step.' in large serif, with 'Final quote before anything is mixed' at top right. Five ascending columns form a staircase, each one a swatch: the price on a coloured cap and a drawn lock of that service's shade hanging beneath. Toner and gloss $45, 45 min, over a violet lock; blow wave from $55 over honey; root colour and refresh from $150, 1 hr 45, over caramel; partial foils from $240, 2 hr 30, over blonde; balayage lived-in from $340, 3 hr 30, over balayage. A gold bar at the foot reads DM me your step.
posts.whyItWorks: Her whole menu as one object, and the staircase does the price anchoring on its own — the eye climbs from $45 to $340 and lands on the colour band where the chair actually earns. Every figure comes from brand.json at render time with the 'from' flag respected, so it cannot drift from what she charges. Friday evening, with the Caulfield Cup the following Saturday, is when a race-day booking gets decided.

caption.hook: Every price, before you have to ask.
caption.body:
Gloss $45. Blow wave from $55. Root colour from $150. Foils from $240. Balayage from $340. Your length and thickness decide the final number, and you get it before anything is mixed.

Caulfield Cup is Saturday the 17th. For colour, book Wednesday the 14th so it has a few days to settle.

howToPost: When someone DMs a step, reply with a real number for their hair, not a range.

posts.title: They followed her
posts.imageAlt: A cream card with a very large gold 10, 'Years. Three suburbs.' beneath it, and a gold arch of drawn honey hair at top right. The route from Malvern to Armadale to Camberwell is drawn as a single lock of hair, dark at Malvern and grown out to gold by Camberwell. Stella McCammon's review is quoted in full in serif. Two green tiles name Nimali Samarakoon, loyal client since 2018, and Uppsala Trinh, client of 10+ years. An ink bar reads 'Some follow a salon. Hers follow her.' and DM to book.
posts.whyItWorks: The strongest proof of 'come for Sha' is not a claim, it is a client who followed her across three suburbs, and that client wrote it herself. The review is quoted in full, verbatim, from reviews.json — spelling and ampersands intact. The two tenure tiles name real clients from her own website and quote nothing, so there is no excerpting of anyone's words.

caption.body: Stella has followed me from Malvern to Armadale to Camberwell. Ten years. Thank you for every single one of them.
caption.cta: If you want to be next, DM me to book.

howToPost: Tag nobody. Stella's words are already on your website, but tagging a client in a promotional post is a step further than she agreed to.

posts.title: Dull by week six?
posts.imageAlt: A deep violet card. 'Dull by week six?' in large serif, cream then lilac, with 'That is the toner fading, not your colour. A gloss puts the tone and the shine back' at top right. Two arches sit side by side: on the left a flat, brassy drawn lock labelled Week six; on the right the same lock glossed to a bright beige blonde with sparkles, labelled After a gloss, in a gold arch. A violet gloss drop and a gold arrow sit between them. A gold bar reads Gloss $45 and DM me, Sundays 11-4.
posts.whyItWorks: The cheapest thing on her menu is the easiest first booking, and most people do not know what it is for. This explains it with a before-and-after that uses nobody's photograph: the same drawn lock, flat and then glossed. It is education with a price attached rather than an offer — $45 is the list price from brand.json, not a discount — and it gives a lapsed colour client a reason to come back between full appointments. Sunday morning, pointing at her Sunday 11 to 4 hours.

caption.hook: Dull by week six? It is probably the toner, not your colour.
caption.body: Toner is what gives colour its exact shade and its shine, and it is the first thing to wash out. A gloss puts both back in 45 minutes. It sits between colour appointments, not instead of them.
caption.cta: DM me for a Sunday gloss, 11 to 4.

howToPost: If someone asks whether they need a gloss or a full colour, ask when their last colour was. Under ten weeks, it is usually the gloss.

videoGuides.title: Three things I will never do to your hair
videoGuides.difficulty: Easy — you, to camera, one take

copyThis.creator: Instagram hook patterns 2026 — the refusal list
copyThis.whatItIs: You, straight to camera, listing three things you refuse to do. It is the talking version of this week's whole idea.
copyThis.whyItCopies: Your top reels are you on camera. This one is only you — no client, no consent to think about — and a refusal reads as expertise rather than selling.
howToCopy: Prop the phone at eye height in the chair you work from. Salon behind you.
Say the first line before you smile: 'Three things I will never do to your hair.'
Hold up a finger for each one. One take.
End on the third and stop — no sign-off.
